differences.title: 1. INITIAL LOAD
differences.leftDesc: Sent as HTML, no JS needed initially for content.
differences.rightDesc: Requires JS to hydrate before content is visible.

differences.title: 2. RENDERING LOCATION
differences.leftDesc: Logic runs on the server, reducing client burden.
differences.rightDesc: Logic runs in the user's browser, consuming resources.

differences.title: 3. DATA FETCHING
differences.leftDesc: Can fetch data directly on the server without API overhead.
differences.rightDesc: Must make API calls to fetch data on the client.

differences.title: 4. BUNDLE SIZE
differences.leftDesc: Reduces client-side JavaScript bundle size as logic is server-based.
differences.rightDesc: Increases client-side JavaScript bundle size due to hydration logic.

differences.title: 5. INTERACTIVITY
differences.leftDesc: Primarily for static content; less dynamic client-side interaction.
differences.rightDesc: Ideal for highly interactive UIs with rich client-side logic.

differences.title: 6. STATE MANAGEMENT
differences.leftDesc: State managed on the server, simpler for server-rendered data.
differences.rightDesc: Requires robust client-side state management for complex UIs.

differences.title: 7. REFRESH BEHAVIOR
differences.leftDesc: A full page refresh might be needed for updates.
differences.rightDesc: Can update specific parts of the UI without full reload.
